Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the intro call today — we left with a clear next step to align on network topology and the on‑prem installer checklist. Per our discussion, IT will run the VPC peering request but needs a bit more detail on IP ranges and whether the private endpoints use static IPs.

Can you share a short technical checklist and a proposed sequencing (VPC peering -> private endpoints -> on‑prem installer validation -> final smoke test)? Also copy of your network diagram would help our security team.

— Sophie

Head of Platform, Orion Labs
[Attachment: orion-current-network.png (referenced)]
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Labs - Private deployment: kickoff

Sophie — thanks, happy to share the plan. Quick answers up front:
- Private endpoints: we prefer stable private IPs behind the customer VPC; we publish NAT'd egress ranges for callbacks but the endpoint itself is accessible via peered routing.
- IP ranges: we'll accept a /20 assigned to our peering connection (we can be flexible).

I attached our initial diagram and a short sequencing proposal. Proposed sequence: 1) VPC peering setup and routing verification, 2) TLS cert exchange and private endpoint deployment, 3) On‑prem installer dry run in Orion sandbox, 4) Full on‑prem install (air‑gapped options if required), 5) Smoke tests + monitoring hook up.

I looped in David (network lead) and Laura (security) to confirm gaps and finalize the checklist.

Attachments: orion-network-diagram-v1.pdf, onprem-installer-checklist.xlsx

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Labs - Private deployment: VPC peering details

Sophie / Rajesh — quick technical notes from our end:

1) Routing & IPs
- We recommend assigning a dedicated /21 for Redwood peering to avoid overlap with future services. If Orion wants a /20 we can accept but will ask for route filters on your side to limit announcement scope.

2) Private endpoint behavior
- The endpoint is a private ALB equivalent inside Redwood’s VPC; once peered, Orion can route directly. We can also support fixed ENI IPs if your firewall rules require them (we'll provision during the endpoint build).

3) MTU & VPN considerations
- If your on‑prem connects via hardware VPN, confirm MTU sizes (we've seen fragmentation at 1400 with some vendors).

4) Certs & Auth
- We'll exchange a service certificate for mTLS; please provide the CA bundle you prefer.

I'll put these items in the checklist spreadsheet. Can we schedule a 45‑minute network deep‑dive early next week with your infra team?

— David
David Kim
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) We currently have a /19 reserved for integrations; could we carve a /21 from that for Redwood?
2) Our security team requires IP allowlist entries for fixed ENIs — if you can provide the ENI IPs prior to final cutover that works.

We can do the network deep‑dive on Tuesday 2026‑07‑14 at 10:00 PT. I've invited our infra folks.

Subject: Re: Orion Labs - Private deployment: security checklist and SOW items

Folks — following up from the technical thread: a few items security needs captured in SOW/controls before we proceed to on‑prem package delivery:

- Audit log export: confirm retention window and S3 destination (we provide a signed endpoint or you can push).
- Key management: confirm KMS/HSM for customer‑facing keys; we support partner‑managed KMS or Redwood KMS.
- Pen test window: we'll coordinate a limited scope penetration test once the sandbox installer is running; please provide POC contact.

I've added these lines to the DocuSign SOW draft (link above). Once Rajesh confirms the /21 allocation and Sophie confirms the cert approach, we can finalize timeline.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
